framing_note: ANALYSIS, not fact. TMICC has not published a 2027-2030 revenue forecast — this scenario is built here from TMICC's own disclosed medium-term guidance (3-5% organic sales growth, from the Strategy tab) compounded forward from the real FY2025 reported revenue base. It is a range for conversation, not a prediction. Kept in its own file for the same reason the Consultant's Brief is separate from the fact tabs.

covid_2020_note.text: 2020 isn't charted as a number here — Ice Cream wasn't yet broken out as Unilever's own standalone reporting segment that year, so no precise like-for-like growth figure exists for it specifically. Unilever's own FY2020 commentary described ice cream as growing 'slightly' overall: out-of-home volume collapsed under pandemic channel closures, offset by a rapid shift toward in-home consumption and 'better-for-you'/plant-based variants (Magnum vegan, Ben & Jerry's lighter Moophoria). Worth remembering as a precedent before assuming channel mix is stable — it has moved sharply before.
covid_2020_note.source: Unilever FY2020 Full Year Results commentary and contemporaneous press coverage

guidance_used.source: Strategy tab — headline commitment 'Growth', set at TMICC's first Capital Markets Day, Sept 2025

caveat: This band assumes organic growth converts cleanly into reported euro revenue. FY2025 is a real, recent counter-example: +4.2% organic sales growth produced essentially flat reported revenue (EUR7.9bn vs FY2024's EUR7.947bn) because currency translation ate the gain. If that pattern recurs, actual reported revenue could land below even the low end of this band despite TMICC hitting its own organic-growth guidance.

drivers_up.driver: AMEA is TMICC's fastest-growing AND highest-margin region (+10.9% OSG FY2025, +7.6% H1 2026, 22.9% Adjusted EBITDA margin) but still only ~25% of group revenue
drivers_up.why_it_matters_for_the_range: Even modest further mix-shift toward AMEA (via the India/Kwality Wall's expansion already underway) lifts both growth and blended margin mechanically, without needing anything to improve elsewhere.

drivers_up.driver: Premiumisation across both indulgence and wellness is a named Group-level growth pillar, not just messaging
drivers_up.why_it_matters_for_the_range: Consumers trading up within a category they're not abandoning supports price-led growth even if volumes stay flat — exactly the pattern already visible in FY2022/2023 (price offsetting weak or negative volume).

drivers_up.driver: Penetration in low-per-capita markets (Pakistan named) and continued emerging-market exposure (30% of FY2024 revenue)
drivers_up.why_it_matters_for_the_range: Structural headroom for volume growth that developed, already-saturated markets (Europe, Americas) don't have as much of.

drivers_down.driver: Currency translation drag — FY2025's real organic-vs-reported gap (+4.2% organic, ~flat reported)
drivers_down.why_it_matters_for_the_range: The single biggest reason the high end of this scenario might not show up in euros even if TMICC hits its organic-growth guidance. A standalone TMICC also has less of Unilever's former treasury scale to smooth this.

drivers_down.driver: GLP-1/weight-loss-drug adoption — a real, named disclosed risk to indulgent ice cream demand specifically
drivers_down.why_it_matters_for_the_range: A genuine two-sided consumer-choice risk: TMICC's own hedge (Yasso, Breyers Carb Smart) is a bet that demand shifts toward better-for-you formats within the category rather than away from it entirely — not yet proven at scale.

drivers_down.driver: Input-cost inflation forcing price-led (not volume-led) growth, as seen in FY2022 (volume -0.7%, price +9.7%) and FY2023 (volume -6.0%, price +8.8%)
drivers_down.why_it_matters_for_the_range: Price-led growth has real limits — FY2023's -6.0% volume shows consumers downtrading when price rises too far, which caps how much pure pricing can carry the range toward its high end.

quotable_insights: Organic sales growth swung from +2.3% to +9.8% in consecutive years (FY2023 to FY2024) — more volatile year-to-year than the 3-5% medium-term guidance suggests once it's averaged out.

FY2025's +4.2% organic growth translated to essentially flat reported revenue (EUR7.9bn vs EUR7.947bn in FY2024) — a real currency-translation gap worth flagging before quoting organic growth figures at face value.

AMEA holds ~25% of group revenue but delivers the highest margin (22.9%) and fastest growth of any region — a real, quantified case that the growth story is currently underweighted in the portfolio, not absent from it.
